Rules / Modernization

SK1023 Use a dedicated System.Threading.Lock

A private readonly object field used only by lock statements can use System.Threading.Lock.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 13.0
Since1.3

Why

C# 13 uses the dedicated Lock API when the lock target has that type. The fix changes both the field type and its object creation, retaining the existing lock statements. It is offered only when all source references are lock targets and the framework provides the Lock API.

Example

Instead of:

readonly object gate = new(); void M() { lock (gate) { Work(); } }

Write:

readonly System.Threading.Lock gate = new(); void M() { lock (gate) { Work(); } }

When it does not fire

Only a single private readonly object field in a class, initialized directly with new object() or target-typed new(), is supported. There must be at least one lock use; every bound reference in the file, including constructed generic types, must be a direct lock target. Monitor calls, aliases, casts, escapes, reassignment, attributes, interior comments and lock bodies containing yields are excluded. Partial containing types and files with directives are excluded so references in another source file or inactive branch cannot escape the proof. C# 13 and a metadata System.Threading.Lock with the required API are mandatory. Reflection-based access to private fields is outside the proof. Shared monitors used for Wait/Pulse are never converted.
